A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UP/TP/WN watermark-removal study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G are readable and support reliable matching, including v2's added Appendix D.3.

before.justification: v1 reports original distillation experiments measuring watermark inheritance, removal effectiveness, knowledge preservation, and computational overhead, with additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments on watermark inheritance with repeated-context masking in Appendix D.3 and Table 11.

M1.justification: UP, TP, WN, watermark stealing, frequency weighting, and adaptive inverse-watermark strength retain their procedures. The expanded access requirements clarify what the existing method already needs; repeated-context masking is an evaluated watermark condition, not a new attack component.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds a teacher-output condition in which repeated contexts no longer receive watermark bias, using SynthID-Text and Unbiased Watermark. This extends the watermark environments evaluated while retaining the QA training task, C4 prompts, English-language coverage, and knowledge benchmarks.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the retained removal and knowledge-preservation experiments are unchanged. Newly evaluated Unbiased Watermark appears in Table 11's inheritance experiment without removal attacks; it is not added as a comparator against UP, TP, or WN.

E3.justification: The added masking experiment specifies storage for 1024 distinct contexts and evaluates both student models without attacks at n = 2 and 3. It retains other main-experiment parameters; the existing training budgets, metrics, and detection procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: v1's Appendix B.2 describes repeated-context masking but does not test its effect on inheritance. v2 adds a focused experimental analysis of that question for SynthID-Text and Unbiased Watermark. Existing ablations, mechanism analyses, multi-source tests, and adaptive-strength experiments remain.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same median detection p-value reporting and statistical formulations. Table 11 follows that existing practice; v2 adds no training-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All 13 existing result tables retain their values after matching renumbered tables. New Table 11 reports masked-condition results: for SynthID-Text at n = 2 and 30k tokens, median p-values are 0.0300 for Llama-7b and 0.0211 for Llama-3.2-1b. These are additional conditions, not revised same-setting performance.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(19), including detector definitions, watermark-stealing scores, weighting, and hash formulations, are retained. The new explanations and clarified access requirements introduce no substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: systematic investigation of watermark removal, effective TP/WN attacks, WN's knowledge preservation and low overhead, and vulnerabilities from multi-source watermark collisions.

C2.justification: Appendix D.3 newly connects masking to reduced watermark-pattern frequency and consequently weaker inheritance, extending v1's discussion of watermark strength and text quality. The principal limitations concerning model coverage, training scale, English tasks, and benchmarks remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new masking experiment's 1024-context storage limit and clarifies required access to training data and both student-model states. It removes v1's code-availability sentence and repository link without replacement; this establishes reduced access information, not that the repository became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 removes the reference to Liu, Sheng and Hu's 'Preventing and detecting misinformation generated by large language models' and expands discussion of already-cited masking approaches. The central positioning against earlier watermark-removal work remains; publication and citation-label updates otherwise refer to retained works.

P1.justification: Several central passages are substantially rewritten or expanded: the radioactivity background, prior-removal discussion, threat model reorganized into four labeled components, computational-overhead discussion, and defense recommendations. v2 also adds D.3 and acknowledgments and revises front matter, while retaining the overall section sequence.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 11 and renumbers the former Tables 11–13 as 12–14. Existing figures and tables retain their designs and content, with changed placement from text reflow. Front-matter formatting changes and printed page numbers disappear.

improvement.justification: The expanded threat model clarifies access already required by the method, and D.3 adds useful evidence about inheritance under previously untested masking conditions. These improve clarity and help readers assess applicability, although they do not extend direct attack validation. Removing the repository link weakens reproducibility guidance, but the overall gains remain modestly positive.
